answer: We formulate a mechanism combining dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices to deter Sybil attacks. Agents invest bonds that are forfeited upon detection of identity duplication, facing a trellis of escalating penalties. On the mesa of strategic interaction, an attacker weighing the expected payoff of Sybil multiplication finds it hollow due to strictly negative returns from capital barriers and equilibrium punishments, thereby converging to a strict Nash equilibrium that resists Sybilization in adversarial multi-agent environments.
